title: EXACT against a column compares with the casing the column stored, not the one loaded
query: EVALUATE ROW ( "r", COUNTROWS ( FILTER ( CaseT, EXACT ( CaseT[Txt], "apple" ) ) ) )

source.quote: so it doesn't store those variations, but refers to the first variation it stored
source.supports: of several casings of one value, the first one loaded is the one kept

source.quote: The first instance of the string is used as the canonical representation
source.supports: the first occurrence is what later equivalent strings are shown as

derivation: Rows 1 to 3 load as apple, Apple, APPLE. The engine keeps only the first variation, apple, and rows 2 and 3 refer to it, so all three rows hold "apple" and EXACT with "apple" is TRUE for each. pear is different. 3 rows.
alternative: If the column kept each row's own casing, only row 1 would match exactly and the result would be 1. If the engine kept a casing other than the first loaded, no row would match and COUNTROWS of the empty table would be BLANK.
